definition: Largess means the generous giving of lavish gifts.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word largess. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know largess should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The wedding was remembered less for its vows than for the groom's largess: cab fare home for every guest and tips that made the waiters blink.
Openhandedness is milder than largess — the openhanded giver gives freely, quietly and without spectacle, while largess showers lavish gifts on a scale meant to be noticed and talked about.
Extravagance goes further than largess — largess at least showers its lavish gifts on people, while extravagance is spending run wild for its own sake.

Bounty is generous abundance handed out — the word carries harvest overtones, plenty flowing to people from a rich source, a good season, a full treasury. Largess is more theatrical: not just plenty, but lavish gifts showered on a crowd, given at a scale meant to be talked about.

Generosity is the everyday virtue of giving freely, at any size and often in private — it asks for no audience and makes no headline. Largess is generosity turned into performance: lavish gifts, plural, arriving in a shower, on a scale people will remember and repeat.

When the copper baron finally sold his mines, the town braced for a quiet exit.
Instead came a season of largess no one had asked for.
He paid off the mortgages on an entire street in one morning.
Schoolchildren found new instruments waiting in the band room, and every teacher received a bonus that made the news two counties over.
